Complementarianism
kom-ple-men-ta´ri-an-izm
n. (the creational order: male and female equal in the image, distinct in office; headship in the house and male eldership in the church)
From complement, that which completes, not compliment. The -arian label is late, a twentieth-century name for what Genesis 1-2 and the household texts already taught. The thing is as old as the rib.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Complementarianism is the creational teaching that man and woman are equal in dignity as image-bearers and distinct in the offices God assigned. Equality is not in dispute: “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Gen 1:27). Distinction is not a bruise of the Fall. It is given before the Fall: “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (Gen 2:18). Paul traces headship to that order, not to local custom: “the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church” (Eph 5:23). The household command is equally plain: “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord” (Eph 5:22). And the church's office is bounded with the same grain: “I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence” (1Ti 2:12). The archetype is not Roman household codes. It is this: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1Co 11:3). Headship in the house is patterned on Christ. Male eldership in the church is the same grain run through 1 Timothy 3. The woman's glory is not a lesser image. It is a different office.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines complement as fullness, completion, whence perfection; and as full quantity or number. The theological name is later; the creational fact is that the woman is given as the help meet who completes the man, not as a duplicate of him.

expand to see more

COMPLEMENT, n. Fulness; completion; whence, perfection.

2. Full quantity or number; the quantity or number limited; as, a company has its complement of men.

3. That which is added, not as necessary, but as ornamental; something adventitious to the main thing; ceremony.

The word in theology is not Webster's -ism. It names the older fact: the sexes complete one another under a head, they do not compete as interchangeable units.

Key Scripture

Gen 1:27 — "So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them."

Gen 2:18 — "And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him."

Eph 5:23 — "For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body."

Eph 5:22 — "Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord."

1Ti 2:12 — "But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence."

Modern Corruption

Equality of image is used to erase distinction of office, and headship is renamed oppression so that the church can copy the world's interchangeable sexes.

expand to see more

Egalitarianism keeps Genesis 1:27 and then files off Genesis 2:18. Male and female become two instances of the same office, and every text that assigns headship is re-read as a local brake on a first-century abuse. Paul will not allow the move. He grounds 1 Timothy 2 in creation and the Fall, not in Ephesus, and he names the husband's headship as the copy of Christ's. If that headship is oppression, then Christ is the oppressor of the church. The argument proves too much, and that is how you know it is wrong.

The other corruption is the harshness that forgets the other half of Ephesians 5. Headship that will not give itself up, that will not nourish and cherish, is not complementarian. It is the old tyranny the gospel came to kill. The husband is the head even as Christ is the head of the church, and He is the Saviour of the body. A man who cites 1 Timothy 2:12 and will not wash feet has not understood the office he is so eager to keep.

Modern sex-revolt goes further than evangelical egalitarianism. It detaches “identity” from the body God created male and female. The dictionary names that as a corruption of Genesis 1:27, not as a pastoral puzzle with two legitimate sides. The image is sexed. The offices are sexed. The gospel does not flatten the sexes. It restores them to their created grain, in the house and in the church.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew zakar / neqebah (H2145, H5347), male and female; ezer kenegdo, a help corresponding to him; Greek kephalē (G2776), head; hypotassō (G5293), to submit.

expand to see more

Hebrew ezer kenegdo (H5828, H5048) — a help meet, corresponding to him; Genesis 2:18, 2:20.

Greek kephalē (G2776) — head; Ephesians 5:23, 1 Corinthians 11:3, Colossians 1:18.

Greek authenteō (G831) — to usurp authority; 1 Timothy 2:12, the verb Paul will not permit a woman over a man in the church's teaching office.

Usage

"“Male and female created he them” — two sexes, one image, no third kind."

"“An help meet for him” — corresponding, not interchangeable."

"“The husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ” — the pattern, not a metaphor you can drop."
